task: Implement a reduced-scope Sun* Kudos board for MoMorph screens MaZUn5xHXZ (live board) and ihQ26W78P2 (Viet Kudo composer modal), SAA 2025. Replace the '/sun-kudos' stub with a public feed (banner, vertical kudos cards, Load more pagination, empty state) and an auth-gated composer modal (recipient autocomplete, plain-text content, free-text hashtag chips). Like/unlike with 'no self-like' and 'one like per user' rules. This is the project's first real DB schema: supabase/migrations was empty before this delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: /sun-kudos renders a static banner, a 'Ghi nhận' trigger pill, and a vertical kudos feed with Load more pagination, publicly viewable with no auth guard on the page itself
Empty state renders the exact copy 'Hiện tại chưa có Kudos nào.' when the feed has zero rows
Unauthenticated click on the 'Ghi nhận' pill or a heart icon redirects to /login; authenticated click opens the composer modal or toggles a like

Composer modal: recipient search-as-you-type (required), plain textarea content (required), free-text hashtag chips min 1 / max 5 (required), 'Gửi' disabled until all three are filled, 'Hủy' discards and closes
On successful submit, the composer closes and the feed refetches page 1 to show the new kudos (not optimistic prepend, per clarifications.md)

Like/unlike: a user cannot like their own kudos (heart disabled), one like per user per kudos enforced by the kudos_likes composite primary key, sender_id/user_id always derived server-side from auth.uid(), never client-supplied

First DB schema for this project: profiles/kudos/kudos_likes tables + auth.users sync trigger + RLS (public read, own-row-only write) written in supabase/migrations/20260908165400_kudos_schema.sql, deliberately NOT applied to any live database in this session (no Supabase CLI available, user applies it themselves)

listKudos fails soft to an empty page (with error logging) on any Supabase error, including the pre-migration 'relation does not exist' state, so the board always renders correctly even before the user applies the migration

e2e-red-first test policy honored: e2e/sun-kudos.spec.ts authored before implementation, genuine RED confirmed (exit 1, 4 real assertion failures against the stub page) before any board/composer/data-layer code existed
Scenarios requiring server-side auth stubbing are documented test.fixme() skips matching the established e2e/home.spec.ts precedent, not faked passes
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npx eslint src e2e, npx jest src, npx playwright test (full suite) all pass with zero regressions to login/home/awards-information/countdown

Explicitly out of scope per the Scope Challenge (clarifications.md): highlight carousel, hashtag/department filters, spotlight word-cloud, sidebar stats/leaderboards/Secret Box, special-day double-hearts, anonymous send, image upload, rich-text formatting/@mention, copy-link/detail-page/profile-page navigation, star badge tiers
blastRadius: Contained to a new feature area (/sun-kudos) plus one new DB schema file. No changes to existing routes' behavior — verified via full regression (all e2e specs, full jest suite, build) with zero regressions to login/home/awards-information/countdown. The DB migration is additive and not yet applied, so it has zero runtime blast radius until the user applies it.
contracts: Server actions (createKudos/toggleLike) derive sender_id/user_id exclusively from server-side auth.uid() via the Supabase server client — never trust a client-supplied id (verified by reviewer, grepped for any client-supplied id param, none found)
'Can't like own kudos' and 'one like per user' are app-layer + DB composite-PK enforced respectively, not a DB CHECK constraint for the former, per clarifications.md's explicit design decision

Contract-mapping shims between phases (receiverId/recipientId, KudosProfile/RecipientOption, nested-to-flat Kudos row shape) live in sun-kudos-client.tsx and were independently verified field-correct by the reviewer

A race condition where two parallel MoMorph UI agents (A1, A2) each independently created src/messages/kudos.json was caught by the orchestrator before integration; both key sets (board.*, composer.*) were manually merged back in and reverified (23/23 component tests) before Phase I1 began
